answer: An agent network can resist Sybil attacks using hardware enclave attestation, requiring nodes to run on a physical secure element no larger than a walnut. The chip provides signed state proofs across each epoch horizon to validate the agent's operational voyage. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of procuring authentic silicon per persona rather than spawning free virtual instances. However, this model depends on centralized chip vendors and remains vulnerable to side-channel leakage.
